newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore Airlines 1st-half net hit by fuel costs.
newsitem.headline: Singapore Airlines 1st-half net hit by fuel costs.

text.p: Singapore Airlines Ltd (SIA) announced on Monday a modest 7.2 percent rise in net profit to Singapore $560.5 million (US$397.5 million) for the six months to September 30, from S$522.7 million the year before.
Group revenue for the national carrier rose 4.6 percent to S$3.53 billion during the period, from S$3.37 billion.
The results were towards the bottom of analysts' forecasts, which had ranged between S$550 million and S$600 million.
An SIA statement said the airline had benefited from an increase in passenger traffic but had been buffeted by escalating jet fuel prices and the strength of the Singapore dollar.
These factors had helped erode its operating yield by 6.7 percent, it said.
SIA said it expected yields to continue to come under pressure during the second half of the year.

"While there may be some respite on the currency front, the direction of fuel prices in the second half is uncertain, as is the recovery of the cargo market," it quoted deputy chairman and chief executive officer Cheong Choong Kong as saying.
SIA carried 5.93 million passengers in the six months to September 30, up 10.2 percent from 5.38 million the year before. Total cargo rose 10.5 to 320,900 tonnes from 290,500 tonnes.
The company said it had continued to add to its carrying capacity through an increase in the frequemcy of flights to some destinations and new passenger and cargo services to others.
It took delivery of two Boeing 747-400s and four Airbus A340-300s during the period April to September, pushing its fleet to 75 aircraft including 34 Boeing 747-400s.
Sales of old or surplus aircraft or spare parts yielded S$122.7 million during the period, up from S$14.7 million the year before.
SIA said its group financial position remained strong with shareholders' funds exceeding S$10.28 billion on September 30.
It proposed a gross interim dividend of 7.5 cents per share, unchanged from the previous year.
